counterfactual_missing_items: No signs of strangulation or bowel obstruction on CT
decisive_items: Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT demonstrated a cluster of small-bowel loops in the left upper quadrant, positioned anterior to the splenic flexure.
The central mesenteric vessels exhibited a spiral (whirl) pattern, with congestion of mesenteric fat and stretching and convergence of vessels.
Differential diagnoses included internal herniation and adhesive bowel obstruction.
response.rationale: R3 directly cites the CT whirl sign and abnormal bowel loop location, which are highly specific for internal herniation, especially in a post-RYGB patient. R4 (ischemia) is contradicted by normal CRP/lactate and no strangulation signs. R2 (adhesive obstruction) lacks CT evidence of obstruction and is only a differential mention. C1 merely appends etiology to R3 without independent raw support.

rejected.why: Imaging suggests ischemia but normal CRP/lactate and no strangulation signs contradict it; less specific than internal herniation.
No CT evidence of obstruction; only generic symptoms and surgical history, not specific to adhesive obstruction.
Append-only completion of R3; no independent raw support beyond surgical history, which is context not diagnostic.
